content:
nina: spinning up bluejay-11b int4 canary on the low-latency pool, will run eval + smoke. keeping defaults for batch/max_new_tokens for now.
sam: saw a 6% drop in exact-match on our date-extraction eval after quant drop-in. small but consistent across prompts.
jordan: also seeing OOMs on two nodes when concurrency hits 10. stack shows repeated slab GC and many small free/alloc churns.
eva: quick repro in canary: single request with max_new_tokens=1024 + microbatching=4 trips an OOM after a few tokens. snippet from runtime: ```ERR OOM: allocate_kv_page size=24MB failed; slab_free_list depth=0; gc_cycles=127```
nina: interesting — we usually run warmstart for kv but bluejay's tokenization gives longer sequences so kv footprint spikes. could explain fragmentation + GC.
sam: quality regression looks correlated with aggressive per-layer quant bias introduced by int4 mapping + per-head scale clipping. metric delta: baseline EM 0.84 -> int4 0.79 on date set.
jordan: hypothesis: quant config + longer effective seq => larger KV churn => more slab fragmentation => occasional allocation fallback path causing token drop / truncation?
eva: dug into decoder outputs — some tokens replaced by low-confidence placeholders on failing runs, looks like micro-timings cause partial cache misses.
sam: plan proposal: 1) roll max_new_tokens default down to 512 for bluejay canary 2) enable kv warmup on first request to pre-alloc moderate pages 3) adjust quant scale clipping for a subset of layers (LN-adjacent) and regen int4 artifacts 4) tweak batch pacing to cap microbatch concurrency per GPU at 6
nina: +1 for lowering max_new_tokens; reduces worst-case memory spike and still covers 95% of product prompts.
jordan: on runtime side, I can land a small GC-smoothing change: fast_free_slab that moves freed small pages to a per-thread reserve (config flag = true for canary). Should reduce global freelist contention.
eva: sample config to try in the canary: ```model: bluejay-11b quant: int4 per_layer_clip: {ln1: 0.006, att4: 0.008} defaults: {max_new_tokens: 512, microbatch_limit: 6, kv_warmup: true, fast_free_slab: true}```
ops-bot: canary deployment queued: deploy/bluejay-11b-int4 -> pool-lowlat-03 by nina @ 1990002000
deploy-bot: health checks passed for 5m, p50 latency +3ms, p95 +12ms, mem used -18% vs int8 baseline (expected), but fragmentation metrics (slab_free_ratio) improved after fast_free_slab flip.
sam: re-run evals on the date-extract suite after patch: EM = 0.83 (int4 with clip tweak + defaults lowered) — still -1% vs int8 but within threshold; quality regressions reduced.
jordan: ran 24h soak under synthetic AA-load with concurrency up to 7: no OOM, slab_gc_cycles down 7x. microburst tailspikes still rare but not fatal.
eva: follow-up: we should add a targeted eval for token-stability (measure token flips under tight timing) into bluejay onboarding CI. saved run: 
```
./evals/run_token_stability.sh --model bluejay-11b --quant int4 --reps 50 --suite date-extract
```
outputs will go to /evals/runs/1990001234-tokenstability.log
nina: action items: sam to finalize per-layer clip changes + regen int4 artifacts (ETA 4h), jordan to land fast_free_slab patch behind flag (ETA 2h), ops to roll the default max_new_tokens->512 for bluejay canary (done), eva to add token-stability test to onboarding CI (ETA tomorrow).
sam: will also add a small note in the model catalog entry: "int4 variant requires reduced max_new_tokens and enabled kv_warmup to avoid GC-induced instability".
jordan: FYI, if we later need to support 1k token flows, we should consider a dynamic kv-page sizing or a transient reservation path instead of big defaults.
nina: thanks team — seems like the combination of quant clipping + memory warmup + smaller defaults gets us back to production-grade. will monitor next 48h and escalate if quality drift reappears. :eyes:
